chunks: And ‘Āṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام used to say: “That I bequeath one-fifth of my wealth is more beloved to me than that I bequeath one-fourth, and that I bequeath one-fourth is more beloved to me than that I bequeath one-third. Whoever bequeaths one-third and leaves nothing behind has gone to excess.”
And he said: “Whoever bequeaths one-third of his wealth and leaves nothing behind has reached the utmost limit.”

key_terms.أُوصِيَ: to make a bequest or will
key_terms.بِالثُّلُثِ: one-third of the estate, the upper bequest limit mentioned here
key_terms.بِخُمُسِ مَالِي: one-fifth of my wealth as a bequest

ai.seo_question: What amount of wealth is recommended to leave as a bequest in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that although bequeathing up to one-third of one’s estate is permitted, a smaller bequest is preferable. It presents one-third as the furthest limit and discourages using it in a way that leaves nothing substantial behind for the heirs.
